axis: a face kept up to impress → a deliberate, overdone pose

members.tone: The mildest word here for faking it, faulting the wish to look good rather than the falsehood itself, which is where *pretence* puts the blame.
Treats the same impression-making pretence as something staged for onlookers, with more of a sneer at the performance than *appearance* carries.
Convicts the pretence of being both calculated and laid on too thick, so the fault is excess as much as falsity.
The flat, general name for putting up a false front, with none of the flattering motive that softens *appearance* and no charge of overdoing it; British spelling.
